name: Hemoglobin H disease

criteria.description: Presence of Hemoglobin H (β4 tetramers) detected by hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Detection of three alpha-globin gene deletions or equivalent alpha-globin gene mutations by molecular genetic testing
Clinical evidence of chronic hemolytic anemia with microcytic hypochromic red blood cells
Presence of splenomegaly on physical examination or imaging
Elevated reticulocyte count indicating increased erythropoiesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of Hemoglobin H on electrophoresis plus molecular confirmation of alpha-globin gene deletions and clinical evidence of chronic hemolytic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by family history and exclusion of other hemoglobinopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Hemoglobin H (β4 tetramers) in red blood cells

heart size increase from chronic anemia

rare.symptomName: Iron overload complications in non-transfused patients

searchTerms: sudden severe anemia triggered by infection
temporary bone marrow failure after infection

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with elevated reticulocyte count
Presence of Hemoglobin H on hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Elevated indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) due to hemolysis
Low mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH)
imaging: Ultrasound evidence of splenomegaly and hepatomegaly
Radiographic bone changes consistent with marrow expansion
other: Peripheral blood smear showing target cells, Heinz bodies, and anisopoikilocytosis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of Hemoglobin H on electrophoresis
Beta-globin gene mutations instead of alpha-globin gene deletions
Different pattern of anemia severity and transfusion requirements
Only one or two alpha-globin gene deletions
Absence or very low levels of Hemoglobin H

redFlags: Signs of iron overload despite no or minimal transfusions
Sudden worsening of anemia or aplastic crisis
references: Higgs DR, Thein SL, Wood WG. 'Alpha-thalassaemia.' Lancet. 2012;379(9813):373-383.
